source.title: Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations
source.authors: Simone Ricci; Niccoló Biondi; F. Pernici

record.tranche_reason: Tests post-hoc orthogonal alignment between independently trained vision-language models and reports residual mismatch and uneven retrieval compatibility. This refines the interchangeability claim by showing approximate, task-dependent alignment rather than complete convergence; it does not test a convergence trend with scale.
record.gate_note: The paper measures paired-model angular discrepancy and retrieval after alignment, so those outcomes bear on V4 and V7. It does not sweep model scale or capability, compare training seeds, or measure recurring features. The geometric theorem is analytical; cited results about latent-space convergence are not this study’s findings.
record.test_reason: A backward-compatibility method paper, but its orthogonal-Procrustes (SVD) baseline directly measures how much retrieval is lost when one VLM's embeddings are mapped into another's space by a fixed linear isometry. It also reports non-negligible residual angular mismatch after alignment. These results bear on V4 (cheap linear interchangeability) and on V7's incompleteness part. The SLERP rows measure the authors' own method and test no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that orthogonal Procrustes gives a useful but approximate alignment that often fails strict backward compatibility. Post-alignment interpolation with the old query exploits the residual geometry, improves over SVD in nearly all settings, and is compatible in 85/90 evaluations versus 45/90 for SVD.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies paired-support orthogonal Procrustes alignment followed by query-side SLERP and evaluates retrieval compatibility; it is not a direct replication of the original convergence measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across model pair, dataset, retrieval direction, and Procrustes support modality. The interpolation weight also affects retrieval; the paper selects weights separately by model pair and retrieval direction, and reports that text-only support is most stable overall.
record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
record.problems: The main retrieval results are point estimates without reported uncertainty. Only five model pairs are evaluated, and there is no scale or capability trend test. Residual angular mismatch is shown in figures without a numeric summary in the text. The per-query oracle uses query-level test labels and is non-deployable.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional per-dataset and per-support-modality Recall@1/5/10 results in Tables 1–6 and additional analyses in Figures 3–12 and Tables 7–9. This record retains the author-reported aggregate, selected R@1 settings showing both successful and failed alignment, and the stated residual-angle result; the remaining detailed benchmark rows are omitted rather than merged into new estimates.

untested.parts: Does not test whether image–caption alignment grows as models improve.
Stitching, relative representations and unpaired alignment not tested; only paired-anchor Procrustes and the affine, ridge and whitened variants.
No comparison of similarity measures or their settings. Support-modality dependence concerns the fitting of the map, not the convergence metric.
No plateau-with-scale test and no test of shared data or objectives as causes. 'Far from complete' is not quantified.

missing.what: Non-isometric alignment baselines generalize much worse than Procrustes: affine 31.69/23.10 R@1, 11/90 compatible; ridge/CCA 14/90; whitened Procrustes 37/90. Bears on the 'simple linear map' part of V4.
Dependence on support modality: e.g. SigLIP1→CLIP ViT-H/14 COCO I2T SVD with image support gives 26.43 vs 43.50 old (text support 41.82).
Zero-shot classification after SVD mapping falls well below the old model (average 51.89 vs 61.99; SigLIP2→SigLIP1 60.79 vs 80.71).
Loss relative to the new model's native performance (e.g. SigLIP2 native Flickr I2T 69.31 vs 42.80 after mapping to the CLIP B/32 gallery) is not recorded.

record.verdict_notes: Only the SVD-alignment baseline and the residual-mismatch figure bear on the claim; the SLERP rows are the study's own method and are unlinked. The original sources (Platonic Representation Hypothesis; Convergent Learning) are only cited as motivation. Main results are point estimates on five model pairs.

versions.untested_parts: No systematic scale or capability sweep, and no test of whether alignment rises as models get larger or more capable.
Evaluates image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval across model upgrades, but does not test whether paired image and caption representations align more as both models improve.
No same-architecture comparisons across random initializations, or analysis of shared features or subspaces across seeds.

Tests paired-data orthogonal Procrustes alignment and retrieval compatibility, but not stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data; does not directly quantify representation-mapping loss across general tasks.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Does not compare measures of representational convergence or test their dependence on similarity-measure settings or out-of-distribution inputs. It compares interpolation operators and support modalities for retrieval, not convergence metrics.
Shows residual mismatch and incomplete compatibility in some settings, but does not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment.

tranche.reason: Alignment-only results demonstrate substantial retrieval losses in some settings and qualify V4. For dimension-reducing pairs, Appendix B describes the map as a partial isometry rather than a full isometry.

Main retrieval results are point estimates; uncertainty appears only in Appendix K's target-subset analysis using three seeds and ±1σ bands.
